content.framing: The human specifies the requirements and checks that the verification is thorough enough. The agent holds the knowledge to implement and to verify. You can open any of the implementation or the evidence, and you do not have to. Hardware on the board, with attached instruments, is a verification layer of its own: where a requirement depends on something outside the design (an optical link, a network card, a data source) it may be the only way to close it.

requirements.title: Each order leaves as one complete 113-byte Ethernet, IPv4 and TCP frame, byte exact against the reference
requirements.text: For any connection state and order, the block sends 15 words (113 bytes without the frame check sequence) whose bytes equal the Python reference, with sequence number, acknowledgement number, window and IP identification captured at the go edge, the SoupBinTCP Unsequenced Data packet of brief 110 as payload, no TCP options and the PSH and ACK flags, including sequence numbers at the 32-bit wrap.

requirements.title: Both checksums on the wire are the RFC 1071 checksums, at the corner cases
requirements.text: The IPv4 header checksum and the TCP checksum of every segment sent equal the reference's, which is itself checked against outside vectors (RFC 1071, a published IPv4 header), including carries in the fold, sums that wrap, a TCP checksum that comes out 0 and a segment whose headers sum to all ones. This is checked by simulation of chosen and random cases; the all-inputs statements are B119-F-CKSUM-IP, -TCP and -MODEL.

requirements.title: Every segment that left is handed back to software, and none that was poisoned
requirements.text: One record (rec_v, rec_seq, rec_len, rec_id, rec_pay) for each unpoisoned segment in the clock of its last word, and none for a poisoned one, so software can retransmit from the records; a segment dropped on the wire is retransmitted by software with the same bytes.

requirements.title: A Python TCP owner and a software OUCH exchange run a whole session through the block
requirements.text: Handshake, SoupBinTCP login, orders, acknowledgements, a dropped segment, heartbeats, a small window and a rejected login all behave as the software side documents, with the exchange seeing every order exactly once and in order.

requirements.title: The RTL lints clean
requirements.text: Verilator -Wall over tcp_fast.sv and the frame builder inside it reports no warnings, with the waivers in lint/lint_waivers.vlt.

requirements.title: The block replaces the order port of brief 110 and works behind its risk logic
requirements.text: With tcp_fast in place of ouch_enter, brief 110's path against brief 110's reference model sends the same orders, with the same payload bytes, valid checksums and gapless sequence numbers; speculative orders that the risk logic refuses leave poisoned.

requirements.title: The register bus and counters behave as the datasheet states
requirements.text: Writes to static fields invalidate the template and are ignored and counted while a segment is in flight; live fields are accepted at any time and restart the staleness age; reads show the registers before the next edge; unmapped addresses read 0; the 14 counters count what the datasheet says and clear on CLR_CNT.

requirements.title: An aborted or unverdicted segment is poisoned and consumes no sequence space
requirements.text: An abort at any of edges 1 to 14 ends the frame with o_poison, leaves SND_NXT and IP_ID as before and produces no record; an abort at edge 0 cancels the go; a speculative segment with no verdict by edge 14 is poisoned; an abort wins over a commit; an abort after the frame left is late, counted and ignored.

requirements.title: The block refuses to send when it is not armed, stale, window-closed, too small or busy
requirements.text: Checked in the order busy, not armed, template not valid or state stale, window closed, MSS below 59, an order is refused with the matching code and counter, nothing leaves and no state changes; a window of exactly 59 bytes admits one segment and one byte less admits none.

requirements.title: The peer sees no gap and no duplicate in the sequence space
requirements.text: Hardware and software share one sequence space. After a heartbeat takes it and gives it back, after an abort, after a refusal and after a retransmission, the peer's received stream has no gap and no duplicate, and nothing is sent by software while the block is armed and idle.

requirements.title: A segment whose payload disagrees with the checksum that was sent is poisoned
requirements.text: The block sums the payload words ouch_enter actually emits and compares the total with the early one the checksum used; a difference (for example a configuration change in flight) poisons the segment and counts sumerr, so a wrong checksum is never sent as valid.

requirements.title: A seeded fault anywhere in the checksum, segment, verdict, refusal or register logic is caught
requirements.text: Every one of the seeded faults of verif/mutants.yaml that builds fails the bench (mutation score 100 percent, 73 of 73). The set is the agent's own; whether it is wide enough is the human's check.

requirements.title: The 96 design's MAC accepts the block's words every clock and corrupts the frame check sequence on o_poison
requirements.text: tcp_fast and mac64_tx of designs/b96_kr260_10g simulated together. A 15-word segment is accepted without a pause, a short poisoned frame is padded as needed and its frame check sequence is wrong, and a good segment's is right. Not simulated yet.
requirements.external: the 96 design's MAC (mac64_tx) and, for the board, the KR260

requirements.text: Software owner against a real TCP stack (a second machine or a network namespace) with a capture compared with the bench's frames. Handshake, data, acknowledgements and the window agree. Not done yet.

requirements.title: The IPv4 header checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs
requirements.text: Brief 119's tcp_fast.sv builds the IPv4 header checksum from a precomputed template plus the changing fields. For all TTL, address and identification values it equals the complement of the ones' complement sum of the header, and the filled-in header sums to 0xFFFF.

requirements.title: The TCP checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs and payloads up to 30 words
requirements.text: For all addresses, ports, sequence and acknowledgement numbers, windows and payloads of up to 30 sixteen-bit words, the checksum the RTL equations produce equals the complement of the ones' complement sum over pseudo-header, header and payload. The byte-pair swapping, the streaming receive check and the timing are not modelled.

requirements.title: The ones' complement arithmetic the checksum equations rest on is correct, for lists of any length
requirements.text: The ones' complement sum of any list of 16-bit words equals the natural-number sum reduced mod 65535, and RFC 1624 equation 3 (incremental update) is correct for a header of any length when the new header is not all zero words; for an all-zero header it gives 0x0000. No current RTL patches a checksum in place; this is the arithmetic the fast path's template-plus-fields form relies on.

designs.notes: Simulation (cocotb on Icarus Verilog 12, one recorded pytest run) and out-of-context Vivado 2026.1 results only. No board run, no MAC of the 96 design in the simulation, no real TCP peer, no real exchange; every order is synthetic. Requirements that need those are hooks and show as not run.

requirements.title: PCS encodes and decodes 64B/66B bit-exactly against an independent model
requirements.text: Scrambler, block encode and decode, gearbox and block lock produce the same bits as the bit-serial Python reference, at every bit offset, with idles, ordered sets and bit-error runs.

requirements.title: 64-bit MAC frames correctly in both directions
requirements.text: Frames start in lane 0 and lane 4, every terminate lane and every length residue is handled, FCS is generated and checked, and a bad FCS is counted.

requirements.title: Block lock is acquired from any bit offset and survives bit errors
requirements.text: The receive gearbox slips to the block boundary from any offset, and a run of bit errors loses lock only above the documented threshold.

requirements.title: The link locks after every receive-datapath restart
requirements.text: At least 100 receive-datapath restarts on the board, each one locks and no restart corrupts a frame.

requirements.title: The default build keeps the board-proven receive path
requirements.text: With RATE_MATCH = 0 the core is equivalent to the core of main 6909e43f (brief 97C) and passes that brief's bench.

requirements.title: Rate matching never corrupts a frame
requirements.text: The elastic buffer inserts and deletes idles only between frames, never under- or overflows silently, and every order sent is fired and passes its content check.

requirements.title: Rate matching holds under a real frequency offset
requirements.text: For any constant receive clock offset from -300 to +300 ppm relative to the transmit clock, no frame is lost or corrupted and the buffer neither overflows nor underflows. IEEE 802.3 allows +-100 ppm at each end, so two compliant ends differ by at most 200 ppm; +-300 ppm gives margin. A loopback has no offset, so a board test needs a second reference clock or another device on the link.
requirements.external: a second reference clock or a 10G network card (a loopback has no frequency offset)

requirements.title: Interoperates with a standard 10GBASE-R network card
requirements.text: The PCS and MAC exchange frames with an independent 10GBASE-R implementation. A PCS talking to itself accepts its own symmetric mistakes, so only another implementation proves the block formats and scrambler order.

requirements.title: Orders are sent only for valid decisions, none is lost or poisoned
requirements.text: Every armed decision yields exactly one order, a poisoned order never fires, and every fault counter stays 0.

requirements.title: The board drivers cannot report OK when a safety check fails
requirements.text: A stale counter, a missing order, a counter that was not read, a wrong polarity or a link that never came up fails the run and names the cause; unsafe actions are refused without the lock.

requirements.title: The laser is off at reset and its polarity is confirmed
requirements.text: tx_disable is 1 at reset; the board run switches the laser on only after the polarity was read back.

requirements.title: Board runs stay inside the recommended operating conditions
requirements.text: Die temperature, VCCINT, VCCAUX and VCCBRAM read from SYSMON are inside the DS925 windows at the start and end of every board run.

requirements.title: No critical clock-domain crossing
requirements.text: report_cdc shows no Critical item and every crossing has the documented synchroniser structure.

requirements.title: The register map is generated from one source and decoded exactly
requirements.text: Every address in regmap.py is decoded, nothing else is, vector widths agree, and the datasheet states unmapped reads return 0, counters read from a snapshot and reads have no side effects.

requirements.title: Every build variant sets only the parameters it documents
requirements.text: The build files set parameters the core has, the base build keeps the 97C defaults, and each variant differs from the base only where documented.

requirements.title: The eye-scan sequencer drives the GT's DRP as its Python twin does
requirements.text: es_ctrl aborts a point on a DRP timeout, latches the point at start, restores every DRP word and is absent when EYESCAN = 0.

requirements.title: A debug build reaches an ILA over the network and leaves the trading path alone
requirements.text: Build dbg_xvc (the eyescan build plus a PS-AXI Debug Bridge and one ILA) closes timing and report_cdc, adds no cell to and removes no cell from the core's hierarchy except the read-only taps, and, on the board, Vivado finds and captures from the ILA over XVC while Linux keeps running. Never part of a build whose latency is measured.

requirements.title: A pointer's gray code changes in exactly one bit per count, at every width
requirements.text: The write and read pointers of rate_match_gp count modulo 2^CW and cross by gray code. For every width CW > 0 and every value, the gray codes of b and b + 1 (including the wrap from 2^CW - 1 to 0) differ in exactly one bit, so a sample taken while the pointer moves is the old or the new code.

requirements.title: Gray decoding inverts gray encoding, at every width
requirements.text: For every width and value, the decoder of the pointer crossing returns the count the encoder was given; and a sampled code that is the old or the new code decodes to the old or the new count.

requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function adder (brief 139a). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. requirements.title: The model is the specification: it equals integer arithmetic
requirements.text: For the divider: the quotient and remainder equal Python integer division for every pair at W = 1 to 8 and for random pairs at W up to 128, division by zero gives all ones and n, and the restoring and non-restoring recurrences equal division step by step with the RTL's register widths.

requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model, exhaustively at small widths
requirements.text: Simulation (Icarus 14) of every variant against the model: every operand pair at W = 2 to 8 (65536 pairs at W = 8), with input gaps; quotient, remainder, order and latency checked.

requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model at large widths
requirements.text: Simulation of every variant against the model: edge-value pairs plus 3000 random pairs (divisors of every magnitude) at W = 16, 24, 32 and 64.

requirements.title: Latency and throughput are what the spec states
requirements.text: The measured latency of every result equals the spec's formula (W + 1, W + 2, ceil(W / PIPE)) for PIPE = 1 to 7 at W = 7, and a pipeline accepts an input on every clock.

requirements.title: The RTL is Verilator -Wall clean
requirements.text: Verilator -Wall --lint-only reports nothing for any variant at W = 8 and 13 with PIPE = 1, 3 and W.

requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults
requirements.text: Each of 16 seeded faults (one text change in the RTL, verif/mutants.yaml) makes the bench fail: killed/total = 16/16. 1 further mutant(s) are equivalent (the same function and timing) and are listed apart with the reason; they are not counted.

requirements.title: Every variant equals an independent reference (SymbiYosys)
requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end: each variant equals an independent reference (SystemVerilog `/` and `%`, the divide-by-zero convention) for all input sequences from reset: 14 jobs at W = 4, 5 and 6, iterative and pipelined, PIPE = 1 to 4; unbounded (abc pdr). Six seeded faults are applied to the RTL and the same proof fails (bounded model checking finds the counterexample), which shows the harness is not vacuous.

requirements.title: Variants of the function agree with each other (SymbiYosys)
requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end, no reference involved: the restoring and non-restoring pipelines give the same output on the same inputs, W = 4, 5, 6; unbounded (abc pdr).

requirements.title: Restoring division is correct for every width (Lean)
requirements.text: The restoring recurrence of div_restoring_*.sv computes n / d and n % d for every width, and for d = 0 returns all ones and n. Proved for all widths in Lean, statement not approved; the Lean text is a transcription of the RTL's step, cross-checked against the Python model for W <= 5; register widths are not modelled.

requirements.title: Non-restoring division with correction is correct for every width (Lean)
requirements.text: The non-restoring recurrence of div_nonrestoring_*.sv, with its final correction, computes n / d and n % d for every width and d > 0 (invariant: a non-negative partial remainder is n - d*Q, a negative one n - d*(Q+1), always in [-d, d)). Proved in Lean, statement not approved; division by zero is not part of this theorem (covered by simulation and the formal reference).

requirements.text: For every variant of the divider there is a build.yaml and an out-of-context clock constraint for xc7a100t and xck26, current against arith/tools/gen_build.py, consistent with the RTL (top, parameters, sources), with the expected primitive use evaluated for each point; the out-of-context wrapper lints clean and is functionally exact for the always-ready variants; the packaged verification harness (harness/run.py, which a user reruns against their own instance) passes on the library instance with every coverage bin hit. requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right
requirements.text: arith/fft/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (NumPy's FFT (forward and inverse), checked for both variants at every N from 8 to 1024, and the identity that the inverse is the swap of a forward transform), and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.

requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model
requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (12 directed or exhaustive points, 8 random ones, across 2 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's: the directed points drive impulses at every position and tones at every bin (small N), DC, Nyquist, a chirp and corner values, forward and inverse, back to back and after the shortest legal gap; the random points drive random frames with random direction and legal gaps up to N = 4096. Each output frame equals the model bit for bit, the latency from in_sof to out_sof equals the formula, and out_valid is N consecutive clocks.

requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not
requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (sdf: (1<<LOGN)-1+LOGN+((LOGN-1)//2)*(TWSTAGES+MULSTAGES+1)+(0 if ORDER else (1<<LOGN)+1); burst: (1<<LOGN)+LOGN*((1<<LOGN)//2+MULSTAGES+3)+1), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.

requirements.title: The properties named in formal/jobs.yaml hold, by proof where the tools allow
requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the properties of formal/jobs.yaml: a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the parameters listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. What the jobs say is in each job's `claim`; parameters beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.

requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults
requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a wrong width) makes the cocotb bench fail, or is argued equivalent in the file's header; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.

requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files
requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.

requirements.title: The burst variant honours out_ready: stalling the sink changes nothing but the timing
requirements.text: With out_ready driven low at random (40 per cent of the clocks) the burst variant's output frames equal the model bit for bit, and out_valid, out_sof and the data stay unchanged in every clock in which out_valid is high and out_ready low. The sdf variant ignores out_ready (stated).

requirements.title: Accuracy against NumPy's FFT is measured and stated, per scaling mode
requirements.text: For each variant, scaling mode and several N and twiddle widths, the error of the model (which the RTL equals bit for bit) against the double-precision FFT of NumPy is recorded in verif/results/accuracy.json: worst and rms error in units of the output LSB, and the SQNR and SFDR for a full-scale tone. The recorded worst error of the scaled mode is at most 6 LSB at every recorded point, and the unscaled mode's SQNR for noise-like input is at least 80 dB at every recorded point with twiddles of 16 bits or more (the unscaled word is W + LOGN bits wide, so its error in output LSBs is large for narrow twiddles: the SQNR is the figure to read); these are the bounds the test enforces, and the figures are what the report states, with no claim beyond them.

requirements.title: A forward transform followed by an inverse transform returns the input within the stated error
requirements.text: Through the RTL (both variants, the scaled mode), forward then inverse of the same frames returns the input divided by N (the scaled mode divides by N in both directions) to within 3 LSB, at the point of the round-trip test; the inverse is the swap of a forward transform, so forward and inverse results are related exactly by the swap.

requirements.title: Fast convolution built on the FFT models equals direct convolution within the stated error (model only, phase 0)
requirements.text: arith/fft_common/fastconv.py (overlap-save and overlap-add on the bit-exact FFT models, both variants) equals numpy.convolve of the same samples and taps to within 8 LSB of the output word (N = 128 to 512, L = 1 to 65 taps, W = 16, TW = 18, WH = 24, FH = 14), the two methods agree with each other within the same bound, a unit filter passes the signal within 3 LSB, and a complex input is filtered part by part. This is a Python model and an interface proposal (docs/fft_suite_plan.md section 5), not RTL: the fast-convolution block is the next phase.

requirements.title: The burst variant honours out_ready, even when both frame banks fill

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function fp_mul (brief 139e). requirements.title: The model is the specification: it equals integer arithmetic
requirements.text: For the rounding and saturation: the three rounding modes equal their definitions on exact fractions for every x, S and W_IN up to 9, the single-adder carry-in form equals the definition for every x, S and mode up to W_IN = 10, the error bounds hold, and saturation and wrap are as specified.

requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model, exhaustively at small widths
requirements.text: Simulation (Icarus 14) of every variant against the model: every input x at W_IN = 5 and 8 for every S, four W_OUT around the rounded width, three modes, wrap and saturate: 954 configurations over the three variants.

requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model at large widths
requirements.text: Simulation of every variant against the model: edge, random and tie-pattern values at W_IN = 16, 24, 32 and 48, six random configurations per variant and width.

requirements.title: Latency and throughput are what the spec states
requirements.text: The measured latency equals the spec (1, 1, 2 clocks) for every variant, one result per clock.

requirements.title: The RTL is Verilator -Wall clean
requirements.text: Verilator -Wall --lint-only reports nothing for any variant at the corner configurations (S = 0, 1, W_IN - 1; W_OUT 2, narrower, equal and wider than the rounded value; all modes, wrap and saturate).

requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults
requirements.text: Each of 14 seeded faults (one text change in the RTL, verif/mutants.yaml) makes the bench fail: killed/total = 14/14.

requirements.title: Every variant equals an independent reference (SymbiYosys)
requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end: each variant equals a reference written from the definitions with wide signed arithmetic for all input sequences from reset: 3 variants x 8 configurations; unbounded (abc pdr). requirements.title: Variants of the function agree with each other (SymbiYosys)
requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end, no reference involved: the fold-add and the increment-after variants give the same output on the same inputs for the 8 configurations; unbounded (abc pdr).

requirements.title: Convergent rounding: carry-in form, error bound and tie-to-even for every S (Lean)
requirements.text: Convergent rounding computed by one addition of the constant 2^(S-1) - 1 and the result's LSB as a carry-in (what fxp_round_fold builds) equals the textbook definition for every integer x and every S >= 1; its error is at most half a unit; a tie goes to the even result. Proved in Lean, statements not approved. Saturation and wrap are not in the Lean model.

requirements.title: Round half up and truncation: definition and error bounds for every S (Lean)
requirements.text: Round half up is floor + [fraction >= half] and errs by at most half a unit; truncation errs by less than one unit and never upward; every x, every S >= 1. Proved in Lean, statements not approved; pure arithmetic, no RTL link.

requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right
requirements.text: arith/mac/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (a structure-free reference that applies the samples one at a time with Python integers) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.

requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model
requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (16 exhaustive points, 12 random ones, across 3 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, runs of ones, and random inputs at the large ones. The function is exact, so there is no error bound.

requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not
requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (dsp: NREG; dsp_cascade: LANES + 1; fabric: NREG), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.

requirements.title: The variants are equivalent to a plain reference, by proof where the tools allow
requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the variants against each other and a plain reference (a single `+` or `*`, or the specification written as RTL). The jobs in formal/jobs.yaml name the widths; a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. Widths beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.

requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults
requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.

requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works
requirements.text: arith/mac/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.

requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files
requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.

requirements.title: A clear-free run adds up modulo 2^ACCW, for every width
requirements.text: For every modulus M and run length, applying samples that never clear gives the initial accumulator plus the sum of the products, reduced modulo M: no saturation, no loss, however long the run. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.

requirements.title: A clear makes the history irrelevant, for every width
requirements.text: Whatever the accumulator held, a sample with clr followed by clear-free samples gives that sample's product plus the others, reduced modulo M. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function mac (brief 139a). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right
requirements.text: arith/multiplier/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (a shift-and-add formulation (and, for the Booth recoding, the digit-sum identity)) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.

requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model
requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (24 exhaustive points, 14 random ones, across 3 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, runs of ones, and random inputs at the large ones. The function is exact, so there is no error bound.

requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not
requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (dsp: STAGES; lut_array: REG; booth_r4: REG), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.

requirements.title: The variants are equivalent to a plain reference, by proof where the tools allow
requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the variants against each other and a plain reference (a single `+` or `*`, or the specification written as RTL). The jobs in formal/jobs.yaml name the widths; a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. Widths beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.

requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults
requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.

requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works
requirements.text: arith/multiplier/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.

requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files
requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.

requirements.title: Radix-4 Booth digits sum to the multiplier's value, for every width
requirements.text: For every multiplier width, the radix-4 Booth digits d_i = -2 b[2i+1] + b[2i] + b[2i-1] of an even-length bit pattern sum, weighted by 4^i, to its two's-complement value. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.source: arith/multiplier/rtl/mult_booth_r4.sv (WBX, NP, bwide, bxe, the digit case table)

requirements.title: An unsigned multiplier extended by a zero bit has non-negative digits summing to its value, for every width
requirements.text: For every pattern whose top bit is 0 (an unsigned multiplier given the RTL's extra zero bit), the Booth digit sum equals the unsigned value. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.

check.framing: The human specifies the requirements and checks that the verification is thorough enough. The agent holds the knowledge to implement and to verify. You can open any of the implementation or the evidence, and you do not have to. Hardware on the board, with attached instruments, is a verification layer of its own: where a requirement depends on something outside the design (an optical link, a network card, a data source) it may be the only way to close it.

requirements.title: Each order leaves as one complete 113-byte Ethernet, IPv4 and TCP frame, byte exact against the reference
requirements.text: For any connection state and order, the block sends 15 words (113 bytes without the frame check sequence) whose bytes equal the Python reference, with sequence number, acknowledgement number, window and IP identification captured at the go edge, the SoupBinTCP Unsequenced Data packet of brief 110 as payload, no TCP options and the PSH and ACK flags, including sequence numbers at the 32-bit wrap.

requirements.title: Both checksums on the wire are the RFC 1071 checksums, at the corner cases
requirements.text: The IPv4 header checksum and the TCP checksum of every segment sent equal the reference's, which is itself checked against outside vectors (RFC 1071, a published IPv4 header), including carries in the fold, sums that wrap, a TCP checksum that comes out 0 and a segment whose headers sum to all ones. This is checked by simulation of chosen and random cases; the all-inputs statements are B119-F-CKSUM-IP, -TCP and -MODEL.

requirements.title: Every segment that left is handed back to software, and none that was poisoned
requirements.text: One record (rec_v, rec_seq, rec_len, rec_id, rec_pay) for each unpoisoned segment in the clock of its last word, and none for a poisoned one, so software can retransmit from the records; a segment dropped on the wire is retransmitted by software with the same bytes.

requirements.title: A Python TCP owner and a software OUCH exchange run a whole session through the block
requirements.text: Handshake, SoupBinTCP login, orders, acknowledgements, a dropped segment, heartbeats, a small window and a rejected login all behave as the software side documents, with the exchange seeing every order exactly once and in order.

requirements.title: The RTL lints clean
requirements.text: Verilator -Wall over tcp_fast.sv and the frame builder inside it reports no warnings, with the waivers in lint/lint_waivers.vlt.

requirements.title: The block replaces the order port of brief 110 and works behind its risk logic
requirements.text: With tcp_fast in place of ouch_enter, brief 110's path against brief 110's reference model sends the same orders, with the same payload bytes, valid checksums and gapless sequence numbers; speculative orders that the risk logic refuses leave poisoned.

requirements.title: The register bus and counters behave as the datasheet states
requirements.text: Writes to static fields invalidate the template and are ignored and counted while a segment is in flight; live fields are accepted at any time and restart the staleness age; reads show the registers before the next edge; unmapped addresses read 0; the 14 counters count what the datasheet says and clear on CLR_CNT.

requirements.title: An aborted or unverdicted segment is poisoned and consumes no sequence space
requirements.text: An abort at any of edges 1 to 14 ends the frame with o_poison, leaves SND_NXT and IP_ID as before and produces no record; an abort at edge 0 cancels the go; a speculative segment with no verdict by edge 14 is poisoned; an abort wins over a commit; an abort after the frame left is late, counted and ignored.

requirements.title: The block refuses to send when it is not armed, stale, window-closed, too small or busy
requirements.text: Checked in the order busy, not armed, template not valid or state stale, window closed, MSS below 59, an order is refused with the matching code and counter, nothing leaves and no state changes; a window of exactly 59 bytes admits one segment and one byte less admits none.

requirements.title: The peer sees no gap and no duplicate in the sequence space
requirements.text: Hardware and software share one sequence space. After a heartbeat takes it and gives it back, after an abort, after a refusal and after a retransmission, the peer's received stream has no gap and no duplicate, and nothing is sent by software while the block is armed and idle.

requirements.title: A segment whose payload disagrees with the checksum that was sent is poisoned
requirements.text: The block sums the payload words ouch_enter actually emits and compares the total with the early one the checksum used; a difference (for example a configuration change in flight) poisons the segment and counts sumerr, so a wrong checksum is never sent as valid.

requirements.title: A seeded fault anywhere in the checksum, segment, verdict, refusal or register logic is caught
requirements.text: Every one of the seeded faults of verif/mutants.yaml that builds fails the bench (mutation score 100 percent, 73 of 73). The set is the agent's own; whether it is wide enough is the human's check.

requirements.title: The 96 design's MAC accepts the block's words every clock and corrupts the frame check sequence on o_poison
requirements.text: tcp_fast and mac64_tx of designs/b96_kr260_10g simulated together. A 15-word segment is accepted without a pause, a short poisoned frame is padded as needed and its frame check sequence is wrong, and a good segment's is right. Not simulated yet.

requirements.title: The IPv4 header checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs
requirements.text: Brief 119's tcp_fast.sv builds the IPv4 header checksum from a precomputed template plus the changing fields. For all TTL, address and identification values it equals the complement of the ones' complement sum of the header, and the filled-in header sums to 0xFFFF.

requirements.title: The TCP checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs and payloads up to 30 words
requirements.text: For all addresses, ports, sequence and acknowledgement numbers, windows and payloads of up to 30 sixteen-bit words, the checksum the RTL equations produce equals the complement of the ones' complement sum over pseudo-header, header and payload. The byte-pair swapping, the streaming receive check and the timing are not modelled.

requirements.title: The ones' complement arithmetic the checksum equations rest on is correct, for lists of any length
requirements.text: The ones' complement sum of any list of 16-bit words equals the natural-number sum reduced mod 65535, and RFC 1624 equation 3 (incremental update) is correct for a header of any length when the new header is not all zero words; for an all-zero header it gives 0x0000. No current RTL patches a checksum in place; this is the arithmetic the fast path's template-plus-fields form relies on.

summary.line: 27 requirements (10 functional, 10 performance, 2 interface, 5 safety); 25 verified, of which 3 rest on delegated acceptances (the planner accepted the Lean statement on the owner's delegation; not human approvals); 2 with no passing evidence; 0 of 2 requirements that depend on an external element closed by hardware; performance verified: 0 on the board, 3 by post-route timing, 7 in simulation only; 0 of 27 requirements agreed by a human, 0 human review(s) recorded; 6 Lean proof item(s) (all widths): 0 with a human-approved statement, 6 with a statement accepted on the owner's delegation (not a human approval), 0 with statement not approved; 3 kernel only, 3 using a compiled decision procedure; build status from: recorded build (not re-run).

designs.notes: Simulation (cocotb on Icarus Verilog 12, one recorded pytest run) and out-of-context Vivado 2026.1 results only. No board run, no MAC of the 96 design in the simulation, no real TCP peer, no real exchange; every order is synthetic. Requirements that need those are hooks and show as not run.

requirements.title: PCS encodes and decodes 64B/66B bit-exactly against an independent model
requirements.text: Scrambler, block encode and decode, gearbox and block lock produce the same bits as the bit-serial Python reference, at every bit offset, with idles, ordered sets and bit-error runs.

requirements.title: 64-bit MAC frames correctly in both directions
requirements.text: Frames start in lane 0 and lane 4, every terminate lane and every length residue is handled, FCS is generated and checked, and a bad FCS is counted.

requirements.title: Block lock is acquired from any bit offset and survives bit errors
requirements.text: The receive gearbox slips to the block boundary from any offset, and a run of bit errors loses lock only above the documented threshold.

requirements.title: The link locks after every receive-datapath restart
requirements.text: At least 100 receive-datapath restarts on the board, each one locks and no restart corrupts a frame.

requirements.title: The default build keeps the board-proven receive path
requirements.text: With RATE_MATCH = 0 the core is equivalent to the core of main 6909e43f (brief 97C) and passes that brief's bench.

requirements.title: Rate matching never corrupts a frame
requirements.text: The elastic buffer inserts and deletes idles only between frames, never under- or overflows silently, and every order sent is fired and passes its content check.

requirements.title: Rate matching holds under a real frequency offset
requirements.text: For any constant receive clock offset from -300 to +300 ppm relative to the transmit clock, no frame is lost or corrupted and the buffer neither overflows nor underflows. IEEE 802.3 allows +-100 ppm at each end, so two compliant ends differ by at most 200 ppm; +-300 ppm gives margin. A loopback has no offset, so a board test needs a second reference clock or another device on the link.
requirements.external: a second reference clock or a 10G network card (a loopback has no frequency offset)

requirements.title: Interoperates with a standard 10GBASE-R network card
requirements.text: The PCS and MAC exchange frames with an independent 10GBASE-R implementation. A PCS talking to itself accepts its own symmetric mistakes, so only another implementation proves the block formats and scrambler order.

requirements.title: Orders are sent only for valid decisions, none is lost or poisoned
requirements.text: Every armed decision yields exactly one order, a poisoned order never fires, and every fault counter stays 0.

requirements.title: The board drivers cannot report OK when a safety check fails
requirements.text: A stale counter, a missing order, a counter that was not read, a wrong polarity or a link that never came up fails the run and names the cause; unsafe actions are refused without the lock.

requirements.title: The laser is off at reset and its polarity is confirmed
requirements.text: tx_disable is 1 at reset; the board run switches the laser on only after the polarity was read back.

requirements.title: Board runs stay inside the recommended operating conditions
requirements.text: Die temperature, VCCINT, VCCAUX and VCCBRAM read from SYSMON are inside the DS925 windows at the start and end of every board run.

requirements.title: No critical clock-domain crossing
requirements.text: report_cdc shows no Critical item and every crossing has the documented synchroniser structure.

requirements.title: The register map is generated from one source and decoded exactly
requirements.text: Every address in regmap.py is decoded, nothing else is, vector widths agree, and the datasheet states unmapped reads return 0, counters read from a snapshot and reads have no side effects.

requirements.title: Every build variant sets only the parameters it documents
requirements.text: The build files set parameters the core has, the base build keeps the 97C defaults, and each variant differs from the base only where documented.

requirements.title: The eye-scan sequencer drives the GT's DRP as its Python twin does
requirements.text: es_ctrl aborts a point on a DRP timeout, latches the point at start, restores every DRP word and is absent when EYESCAN = 0.

requirements.title: A debug build reaches an ILA over the network and leaves the trading path alone
requirements.text: Build dbg_xvc (the eyescan build plus a PS-AXI Debug Bridge and one ILA) closes timing and report_cdc, adds no cell to and removes no cell from the core's hierarchy except the read-only taps, and, on the board, Vivado finds and captures from the ILA over XVC while Linux keeps running. Never part of a build whose latency is measured.

requirements.title: A pointer's gray code changes in exactly one bit per count, at every width
requirements.text: The write and read pointers of rate_match_gp count modulo 2^CW and cross by gray code. For every width CW > 0 and every value, the gray codes of b and b + 1 (including the wrap from 2^CW - 1 to 0) differ in exactly one bit, so a sample taken while the pointer moves is the old or the new code.

requirements.title: Gray decoding inverts gray encoding, at every width
requirements.text: For every width and value, the decoder of the pointer crossing returns the count the encoder was given; and a sampled code that is the old or the new code decodes to the old or the new count.

requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right
requirements.text: arith/adder/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (a bit-serial chain of full adders) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.

requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model
requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (16 exhaustive points, 14 random ones, across 3 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, runs of ones, and random inputs at the large ones. The function is exact, so there is no error bound.

requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not
requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (ripple: 0; carry_select: 0; pipelined: STAGES), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.

requirements.title: The variants are equivalent to a plain reference, by proof where the tools allow
requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the variants against each other and a plain reference (a single `+` or `*`, or the specification written as RTL). The jobs in formal/jobs.yaml name the widths; a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. Widths beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.

requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults
requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.

requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works
requirements.text: arith/adder/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.

requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files
requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.

requirements.title: Carry-select composition adds, for every width
requirements.text: A carry-select adder (a low block, and a high block computed for carry in 0 and 1 and selected by the low block's carry out) returns the same sum and carry out as plain addition, for every block widths m and k and every pair of operands. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.source: arith/adder/rtl/adder_carry_select.sv (g_first and g_sel blocks, two blocks)

requirements.title: Subtraction is addition of the complements, for every width
requirements.text: For every width n, a + ~b + ~bin on n bits equals a - b - bin modulo 2^n, and its carry out is 1 exactly when there is no borrow: the identity every variant's subtract path rests on. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function adder (brief 139a). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.title: The model is the specification: it equals integer arithmetic
requirements.text: For the divider: the quotient and remainder equal Python integer division for every pair at W = 1 to 8 and for random pairs at W up to 128, division by zero gives all ones and n, and the restoring and non-restoring recurrences equal division step by step with the RTL's register widths.

requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model, exhaustively at small widths
requirements.text: Simulation (Icarus 14) of every variant against the model: every operand pair at W = 2 to 8 (65536 pairs at W = 8), with input gaps; quotient, remainder, order and latency checked.

requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model at large widths
requirements.text: Simulation of every variant against the model: edge-value pairs plus 3000 random pairs (divisors of every magnitude) at W = 16, 24, 32 and 64.

requirements.title: Latency and throughput are what the spec states
requirements.text: The measured latency of every result equals the spec's formula (W + 1, W + 2, ceil(W / PIPE)) for PIPE = 1 to 7 at W = 7, and a pipeline accepts an input on every clock.

requirements.title: The RTL is Verilator -Wall clean
requirements.text: Verilator -Wall --lint-only reports nothing for any variant at W = 8 and 13 with PIPE = 1, 3 and W.

requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults
requirements.text: Each of 16 seeded faults (one text change in the RTL, verif/mutants.yaml) makes the bench fail: killed/total = 16/16. 1 further mutant(s) are equivalent (the same function and timing) and are listed apart with the reason; they are not counted.

requirements.title: Every variant equals an independent reference (SymbiYosys)
requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end: each variant equals an independent reference (SystemVerilog `/` and `%`, the divide-by-zero convention) for all input sequences from reset: 14 jobs at W = 4, 5 and 6, iterative and pipelined, PIPE = 1 to 4; unbounded (abc pdr). Six seeded faults are applied to the RTL and the same proof fails (bounded model checking finds the counterexample), which shows the harness is not vacuous.

requirements.title: Variants of the function agree with each other (SymbiYosys)
requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end, no reference involved: the restoring and non-restoring pipelines give the same output on the same inputs, W = 4, 5, 6; unbounded (abc pdr).

requirements.title: Restoring division is correct for every width (Lean)
requirements.text: The restoring recurrence of div_restoring_*.sv computes n / d and n % d for every width, and for d = 0 returns all ones and n. Proved for all widths in Lean, statement not approved; the Lean text is a transcription of the RTL's step, cross-checked against the Python model for W <= 5; register widths are not modelled.

requirements.title: Non-restoring division with correction is correct for every width (Lean)
requirements.text: The non-restoring recurrence of div_nonrestoring_*.sv, with its final correction, computes n / d and n % d for every width and d > 0 (invariant: a non-negative partial remainder is n - d*Q, a negative one n - d*(Q+1), always in [-d, d)). requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right
requirements.text: arith/fft/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (NumPy's FFT (forward and inverse), checked for both variants at every N from 8 to 1024, and the identity that the inverse is the swap of a forward transform), and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.

requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model
requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (12 directed or exhaustive points, 8 random ones, across 2 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's: the directed points drive impulses at every position and tones at every bin (small N), DC, Nyquist, a chirp and corner values, forward and inverse, back to back and after the shortest legal gap; the random points drive random frames with random direction and legal gaps up to N = 4096. Each output frame equals the model bit for bit, the latency from in_sof to out_sof equals the formula, and out_valid is N consecutive clocks.

requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not
requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (sdf: (1<<LOGN)-1+LOGN+((LOGN-1)//2)*(TWSTAGES+MULSTAGES+1)+(0 if ORDER else (1<<LOGN)+1); burst: (1<<LOGN)+LOGN*((1<<LOGN)//2+MULSTAGES+3)+1), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.

requirements.title: The properties named in formal/jobs.yaml hold, by proof where the tools allow
requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the properties of formal/jobs.yaml: a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the parameters listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. What the jobs say is in each job's `claim`; parameters beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.

requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults
requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a wrong width) makes the cocotb bench fail, or is argued equivalent in the file's header; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.

requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files
requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.

requirements.title: The burst variant honours out_ready: stalling the sink changes nothing but the timing
requirements.text: With out_ready driven low at random (40 per cent of the clocks) the burst variant's output frames equal the model bit for bit, and out_valid, out_sof and the data stay unchanged in every clock in which out_valid is high and out_ready low. The sdf variant ignores out_ready (stated).

requirements.title: Accuracy against NumPy's FFT is measured and stated, per scaling mode
requirements.text: For each variant, scaling mode and several N and twiddle widths, the error of the model (which the RTL equals bit for bit) against the double-precision FFT of NumPy is recorded in verif/results/accuracy.json: worst and rms error in units of the output LSB, and the SQNR and SFDR for a full-scale tone. The recorded worst error of the scaled mode is at most 6 LSB at every recorded point, and the unscaled mode's SQNR for noise-like input is at least 80 dB at every recorded point with twiddles of 16 bits or more (the unscaled word is W + LOGN bits wide, so its error in output LSBs is large for narrow twiddles: the SQNR is the figure to read); these are the bounds the test enforces, and the figures are what the report states, with no claim beyond them.

requirements.title: A forward transform followed by an inverse transform returns the input within the stated error
requirements.text: Through the RTL (both variants, the scaled mode), forward then inverse of the same frames returns the input divided by N (the scaled mode divides by N in both directions) to within 3 LSB, at the point of the round-trip test; the inverse is the swap of a forward transform, so forward and inverse results are related exactly by the swap.

requirements.title: Fast convolution built on the FFT models equals direct convolution within the stated error (model only, phase 0)
requirements.text: arith/fft_common/fastconv.py (overlap-save and overlap-add on the bit-exact FFT models, both variants) equals numpy.convolve of the same samples and taps to within 8 LSB of the output word (N = 128 to 512, L = 1 to 65 taps, W = 16, TW = 18, WH = 24, FH = 14), the two methods agree with each other within the same bound, a unit filter passes the signal within 3 LSB, and a complex input is filtered part by part. This is a Python model and an interface proposal (docs/fft_suite_plan.md section 5), not RTL: the fast-convolution block is the next phase.

requirements.title: Accuracy against NumPy is measured beside the scaled and unscaled modes, and the stated bound holds
requirements.text: For both architectures, every N from 8 to 4096 and four input levels (0, -20, -40 and -60 dB of a full-scale noise-like frame), the error of the bit-exact model (which the RTL equals) against numpy.fft is recorded in verif/results/accuracy.json for the block-floating-point mode, the scaled mode and the unscaled mode (worst and rms error in the mode's own output LSB, and the SQNR). The bound is: the error of every part is at most the unscaled core's own worst error plus 2**exponent (the final rounding at the frame's exponent); it holds at every recorded point. The recorded SQNR of the block-floating-point mode at full level is at least 80 dB, its worst error at full level at most 2 output LSB, and at -60 dB its SQNR is at least 30 dB where the scaled mode's is negative.

requirements.title: Every exponent range is visited and the exponent word is bit exact
requirements.text: Frames of very different level (all zero, one LSB, noise at six amplitudes, a loud and a quiet tone, the most negative value, a frame whose bin 0 is 2**W - 1 so that the rounding carries and the word saturates) are sent through both architectures; each output frame and its exponent equal the model, the frames reach at least six different exponents, and the exponent is the same on every word of its frame and travels with the data when frames follow each other at different levels.

requirements.text: With out_ready low in 40 per cent of the clocks, and again in 92 per cent (reading a frame then takes longer than the core needs for the next, so both banks fill and the core must wait), the burst variant's frames, exponents and order equal the model, and out_valid, out_sof, the data and the exponent stay unchanged in every clock in which out_valid is high and out_ready low. requirements.title: Rounding increment carries into the exponent, for every width
requirements.text: For a packed pattern e * m + f with fraction f < m (m = 2^MAN), adding the rounding increment 1 either raises the fraction by one or, when the fraction is all ones, raises the exponent by one and leaves a zero fraction: the identity fp_pack's single add on the packed {exponent, fraction} pattern rests on, so a significand overflow, a subnormal rounding up to the smallest normal number and a largest finite number rounding up to infinity need no special case. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.source: arith/fp_common/fp_pack.sv (wsum: the increment added to the packed pattern)

requirements.title: Normalising left by NW - 1 - msb puts the leading one at the top, for every width
requirements.text: For a value v with its leading one at bit k (2^k <= v < 2^(k+1)) and k < NW, shifting left by NW - 1 - k places gives a value in [2^(NW-1), 2^NW): the leading one is at bit NW - 1, which is what fp_norm's count lz = NW - 1 - msb does. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.source: arith/fp_common/fp_norm.sv (the shift by the leading-zero count)

requirements.title: The rounding decision is round-to-nearest, ties to even, for every width
requirements.text: For a kept part hi and a discarded part lo below the threshold 2h, incrementing hi exactly when lo > h, or lo = h and hi is odd (the guard-and-sticky rule of fp_pack), gives a value within h of the exact one and, when it is exactly h away, even. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.

Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.

requirements.title: Rounding increment carries into the exponent, for every width
requirements.text: For a packed pattern e * m + f with fraction f < m (m = 2^MAN), adding the rounding increment 1 either raises the fraction by one or, when the fraction is all ones, raises the exponent by one and leaves a zero fraction: the identity fp_pack's single add on the packed {exponent, fraction} pattern rests on, so a significand overflow, a subnormal rounding up to the smallest normal number and a largest finite number rounding up to infinity need no special case. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.source: arith/fp_common/fp_pack.sv (wsum: the increment added to the packed pattern)

requirements.title: Normalising left by NW - 1 - msb puts the leading one at the top, for every width
requirements.text: For a value v with its leading one at bit k (2^k <= v < 2^(k+1)) and k < NW, shifting left by NW - 1 - k places gives a value in [2^(NW-1), 2^NW): the leading one is at bit NW - 1, which is what fp_norm's count lz = NW - 1 - msb does. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.source: arith/fp_common/fp_norm.sv (the shift by the leading-zero count)

requirements.title: The rounding decision is round-to-nearest, ties to even, for every width
requirements.text: For a kept part hi and a discarded part lo below the threshold 2h, incrementing hi exactly when lo > h, or lo = h and hi is odd (the guard-and-sticky rule of fp_pack), gives a value within h of the exact one and, when it is exactly h away, even. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function fp_fma (brief 139e). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right
requirements.text: arith/fp_mul/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (an enumeration of every finite value of a tiny format (the nearest one, ties to even) and NumPy's hardware float32 multiplication) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.

requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model
requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (16 exhaustive points, 12 random ones, across 2 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, runs of ones, and random inputs at the large ones. The function is exact, so there is no error bound.

requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not
requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (dsp: STAGES; lut: STAGES), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.

requirements.title: The variants are equivalent to a plain reference, by proof where the tools allow
requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the variants against each other and a plain reference (a single `+` or `*`, or the specification written as RTL). The jobs in formal/jobs.yaml name the widths; a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. Widths beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.

requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults
requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.

requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works
requirements.text: arith/fp_mul/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.

requirements.title: The model is the specification: it equals integer arithmetic
requirements.text: For the rounding and saturation: the three rounding modes equal their definitions on exact fractions for every x, S and W_IN up to 9, the single-adder carry-in form equals the definition for every x, S and mode up to W_IN = 10, the error bounds hold, and saturation and wrap are as specified.

requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model, exhaustively at small widths
requirements.text: Simulation (Icarus 14) of every variant against the model: every input x at W_IN = 5 and 8 for every S, four W_OUT around the rounded width, three modes, wrap and saturate: 954 configurations over the three variants.

requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model at large widths
requirements.text: Simulation of every variant against the model: edge, random and tie-pattern values at W_IN = 16, 24, 32 and 48, six random configurations per variant and width.

requirements.title: Latency and throughput are what the spec states
requirements.text: The measured latency equals the spec (1, 1, 2 clocks) for every variant, one result per clock.

requirements.title: The RTL is Verilator -Wall clean
requirements.text: Verilator -Wall --lint-only reports nothing for any variant at the corner configurations (S = 0, 1, W_IN - 1; W_OUT 2, narrower, equal and wider than the rounded value; all modes, wrap and saturate).

requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults
requirements.text: Each of 14 seeded faults (one text change in the RTL, verif/mutants.yaml) makes the bench fail: killed/total = 14/14.

requirements.title: Every variant equals an independent reference (SymbiYosys)
requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end: each variant equals a reference written from the definitions with wide signed arithmetic for all input sequences from reset: 3 variants x 8 configurations; unbounded (abc pdr). Six seeded faults are applied to the RTL and the same proof fails (bounded model checking finds the counterexample), which shows the harness is not vacuous.

requirements.title: Variants of the function agree with each other (SymbiYosys)
requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end, no reference involved: the fold-add and the increment-after variants give the same output on the same inputs for the 8 configurations; unbounded (abc pdr).

requirements.title: Convergent rounding: carry-in form, error bound and tie-to-even for every S (Lean)
requirements.text: Convergent rounding computed by one addition of the constant 2^(S-1) - 1 and the result's LSB as a carry-in (what fxp_round_fold builds) equals the textbook definition for every integer x and every S >= 1; its error is at most half a unit; a tie goes to the even result. Proved in Lean, statements not approved. Saturation and wrap are not in the Lean model.

requirements.title: Round half up and truncation: definition and error bounds for every S (Lean)
requirements.text: Round half up is floor + [fraction >= half] and errs by at most half a unit; truncation errs by less than one unit and never upward; every x, every S >= 1. Proved in Lean, statements not approved; pure arithmetic, no RTL link.

requirements.title: Out-of-context build descriptions are prepared for Artix-7 and K26 (not run)
requirements.text: For every variant of the rounding and saturation there is a build.yaml and an out-of-context clock constraint for xc7a100t and xck26, current against arith/tools/gen_build.py, consistent with the RTL (top, parameters, sources), with the expected primitive use evaluated for each point; the out-of-context wrapper lints clean and is functionally exact for the always-ready variants; the packaged verification harness (harness/run.py, which a user reruns against their own instance) passes on the library instance with every coverage bin hit. No Vivado run has been made: this requirement is about preparation, not about area, Fmax or power.
